videos.description:
What was life really like at every rank in the Roman Empire’s army?

In this immersive POV documentary, you’ll experience the Roman military hierarchy from the bottom to the top — beginning as a Tiro, an inexperienced recruit learning to march, drill, dig, and survive Roman discipline, before progressing through increasingly powerful positions inside the legion.

You’ll experience life as a Miles Gregarius, Tesserarius, Signifer, Optio, Centurion, Senior Centurion, Primus Pilus, Praefectus Castrorum, Tribunus Laticlavius, and finally Legatus Legionis — commander of an entire Roman legion.

But rising through Rome’s army wasn’t simply about becoming a better fighter. Each level brought more authority, responsibility, pressure, and consequences. At the bottom, one mistake could cost you your life. At the top, one decision could affect thousands of soldiers.

This video explores Roman army ranks, legionary training, military discipline, command structure, daily life, battlefield responsibilities, logistics, and the complicated career paths that existed inside the Roman Empire’s military system.

From carrying a shield and digging camps to commanding an entire legion — this is your life as every rank in the Roman Empire’s army.

Your Life as Every Rank in the Hells Angels

What changes as you move from a Hells Angels supporter to a full-patch member—and eventually into local charter leadership?

This immersive POV documentary explores Hells Angels membership stages and officer roles through second-person storytelling. Experience the uncertainty of hanging around, the demands of prospecting, the responsibilities of membership, and the pressures that come with a seat at the head of the table.

We explore supporters, hangarounds, prospects, full-patch members, road captains, secretaries, treasurers, sergeants-at-arms, vice presidents, and charter presidents.

These positions are not one universal promotion ladder. Officer roles carry different responsibilities, practices vary between charters, and advancement is never guaranteed.
